name: cue-anchored-memory
description: Use when you are about to record a situational operational fact for future sessions: a gotcha, a local convention, a "never do X when touching Y". Such facts fail by not being delivered, not by not being stored, so give each one a trigger condition (path, symbol, semantic, event or temporal cue) and the most deterministic delivery this system has: an enforcing check, a cue-fired hook injection proposed to the operator, or at minimum an always-loaded index line. Never leave a load-bearing fact in a file that is read only when the agent chooses to, and never install a hook yourself. Write the reason beside each fact so that a later editor can retire it. Distinct from memory-hubness-gate and memory-use-warrant, which guard vector-memory writes and the use of recalled memory. Backed by the cue-anchored memory model (arxiv 2607.20972) and the catastrophic-remembering analysis (arxiv 2608.11095). Triggers on saving a gotcha or convention to memory and on pruning an always-loaded file.
